result.topic_en: Gauss tabulates sequences of residue patterns (0/+ combinations) modulo primes and the number of roots, to determine how many roots of $(x+1)^{\frac{p-1}{2}} \mp (x \pm 1)^{\frac{p-1}{2}}$ exist, with side notes on factors of the forms $4n+1$, $4n+2$.

methods.what: Tabulation of residue patterns (successions of quadratic residues/non-residues) against counts, used to bound the number of roots of a polynomial congruence
methods.quote:
